conventions.convention: Mean zero means zero total surface integral over the whole boundary, including when the boundary is disconnected. The operator extension kills the global constant and has mean-zero range; its kernel has zero mean in each variable.
The NtD observation is right-smoothed: Aγ = Rγ(1−ΔM)^(−r_d/2), where r_d = (d−1)/2−1+τ, τ=1/2 for d=2 and any fixed τ>0 for d≥3.
Boundary spectral Sobolev norms use weights (1+λj)^s in their squared coefficient norm; zero eigenvalues beyond the global constant remain in the mean-zero spectral space.
Neumann fluxes act through the continuous conjugate-linear dual of the trace quotient by constants. Conductivities are real and uniformly elliptic; conormal flux is outward.
Complex kernel L2 is treated as a real Hilbert space; realification sends f to (Re f, Im f) isometrically, and the approximating generalized FNO has two real input channels.
The transferred inverse modulus contains the square root of kernel distance: ω⋆(s)=C0[log(1/min{C1√s,t0})]^(−ρ), with value zero at zero and a sufficiently small saturation cutoff.
Noise ranges over Kδ={η∈K:‖η‖2≤δ} for a compact set K in the continuum kernel space; an arbitrary bounded noise ball is not assumed compact.
The activation is fixed, smooth, globally Lipschitz and nonpolynomial. Fourier multipliers preserve real fields by conjugate symmetry; periodic coordinate biases are allowed.
The arbitrary-subset Hilbert extension assumes full Axiom of Choice, used through Zorn's lemma; the ball-intersection proof also explicitly assumes it.

load_bearing.statement: For γ∈X_d(R), the extended smoothed NtD observation is Hilbert–Schmidt with a unique zero-mean-in-each-variable L2 kernel of equal norm, uniformly bounded over the class. Moreover, ‖dotΛγ−dotΛγ0‖≤C‖κγ−κγ0‖2^(1/2).

Under the stated smooth-domain, fixed-background-collar and ellipticity assumptions, Rγ maps mean-zero L2 fluxes uniformly into spectral H1; Rγ−R1 maps mean-zero H^(−1/2) fluxes into every integer spectral Hq, and NtD difference matrix entries satisfy |bij|≤CL(wiwj)^(−L) for every L>0.

Assume the Axiom of Choice. A map from any subset of a real Hilbert space into a real Hilbert space that satisfies a continuous nondecreasing concave modulus vanishing at zero extends to the whole source Hilbert space with the same modulus.

Assume Countable Choice. For the stated smooth EIT boundary product, every continuous T:L2(M;R^a)→L2(Ω;R^b) is uniformly approximable on every compact input set to every positive tolerance by a generalized FNO with a fixed smooth globally Lipschitz nonpolynomial activation.

X2(R) is compact in L1(Ω), and X_d(R) for d≥3 is compact in C1 of the closed domain. The kernel map has the stated Lq Lipschitz estimate in dimension two and is continuous in C1 for d≥3; consequently its exact image is compact in boundary-product L2.

Assume the Axiom of Choice. For arbitrary Hilbert-space families satisfying ‖yi−yj‖≤ω(‖xi−xj‖), where ω is continuous, nondecreasing, concave and zero at zero, the intersection of the closed balls with centers yi and radii ω(‖xi−x‖) is nonempty. The empty-index intersection is all of the target Hilbert space.

Assume Countable Choice. The stated compact smooth boundary product admits bounded chart localization and reassembly maps G,L with LG=I, compact-uniform Fourier projection convergence, and the stated H1-to-L2 Fourier-tail bound.
